unit: R-AUTH (W1-4 server: W1-4b type classifier, W1-4c no server auto-refresh, flag-ON logout by access token, ruling-2 expired-bearer logout; W1-9b atomic lockout arming + non-positive-TTL re-arm). Worktree C:/Users/SynAckITPC/Documents/AI/sc-r-auth, branch retro/w1-4-w1-9-auth, wip f8481f62 on base 1c6f6796.

defects.claim: With ENABLE_LOGOUT_UPSTREAM_REVOCATION on, the expired-bearer logout branch lets an UNAUTHENTICATED caller trigger an upstream gotrue POST /auth/v1/token (refresh grant), a Redis SETEX and a WARNING on every request, with no rate limit. A made-up JWT whose exp is in the past (any signature) plus any refresh_token string qualifies, because the signature is never verified. /auth/logout has no @limiter.limit. slowapi's decorator check sits inside the endpoint, which never runs here because get_current_user raises first, so even a future decorator would not cover this branch. Every other route that reaches the token endpoint without auth (register 3/min, login 5/min, refresh 10/min, social 10/min) is throttled. Reproduced through the real app and the real pinned SDK against a loopback gotrue: flag OFF gave 3/3 401 and 0 upstream calls. Flag ON, 40 forged requests gave 40x 200, 40 upstream POST /token, 40 distinct Redis blacklist writes and 40 '[auth] logout upstream leg failed' WARNINGs. The same volume on /auth/refresh gave 10x 401 and 30x 429.
defects.why_it_matters: The reviewer measured that Supabase's refresh-grant rate limit is per IP, and every refresh from the fleet leaves from the one Railway IP. This branch turns the logout route into an unauthenticated, unthrottled way to spend that shared budget. Legitimate refreshes then get 429, which W1-4b now maps to 503, so users cannot refresh. It also costs one billed Upstash write per request and floods the exact WARNING line the activation canary counts ('about 0 expected'). The flag is default OFF, so this does not block merging. It does block flipping the flag. Fix options: a limiter check inside _LogoutRoute's expired branch (for example limiter.limit applied to a helper, or a manual Redis-counter per client key) with the /auth/refresh budget; also skip _revoke_token for a JWT that fails a cheap structural check.

defects.location: app/services/auth_service.py track_failed_login (SET key 0 NX EX 900 then INCR) and check_account_locked (re-arm only when count >= threshold)
defects.claim: Two TTL-less counter paths remain, and the green acknowledged both. (a) A legacy key already stuck in prod Redis with TTL -1 and count below 5: SET NX does nothing on an existing key, so INCR keeps it TTL-less. Failures months apart still add up to a lock. Probe B: seed count 3 with no TTL, one failure 30 days later gives attempts 4 and ttl -1, one more 30 days after that gives locked True, then a 900 s window. (b) A key that expires between SET NX and INCR: INCR recreates it without a TTL. Probe C, where the fake clock advances 2 s before INCR, gives value 1 and ttl -1. Both end in a re-armed 15-minute lock, never a permanent one, so the ruling's 'never permanent' holds. The reviewer's 'five failures over ANY span lock the account' still holds for these keys.
defects.why_it_matters: A user with a legacy stuck key at count 4 is locked for 15 minutes by one mistyped password, whenever it happens. A one-line EXPIRE key window NX after INCR (upstash-redis 1.7.0 and redis-py both support it) would close both paths. Not a merge blocker.

tests_that_prove_nothing: The green says W1-4b returns the categoriser's transient dict 'byte for byte', but no test pins it. Mutant N_transient_msg_changed changed the refresh_session transient dict's error text from 'Connection failed. Please try again.' to 'Upstream down.' (which changes the 503 body's error field). Result: all 123 unit tests passed. No node asserts the 503 body text.

The 'TYPE only, never the text' backstop in _logout_with_expired_bearer is unpinned. Mutant N_expired_backstop_raw_e logged the raw exception there, and 123 passed. The same holds for the new refresh-path WARNING: mutant N_transient_log_raw_e logged the raw e instead of type(e).__name__, and 123 passed. These are the same class of gap as the reviewer's M7: logout_user swallows everything, so the backstop cannot be reached and no test ever reaches it.

test_retro_w1_4_logout_expired.py::test_flag_on_only_an_expired_jwt_takes_the_expired_branch[unexpired_but_rejected] and test_unverified_expiry_parser_edges only use tokens 5 s or 3600 s from expiry. Mutant N_exp_window_plus60 (exp <= time.time() + 60) survived with 123 passed. The boundary that stops a revoked-but-unexpired token from taking the expired branch is not pinned near the edge.

Mutant N_route_any_status, which drops the status_code != 401 guard in _LogoutRoute, survived with 123 passed. On this route that guard is effectively equivalent today, because get_current_user raises only 401 HTTPExceptions. This entry records the survivor; it is not a real gap.
summary:

**Unit re-run: no mutant on disk.** The 5 unit files on the pinned venv, with a process-wide non-loopback socket guard loaded via -p before conftest, gave 123 passed and 0 guard attempts. This equals the green's recorded 123; the prompt's 'close re-run' count was undefined. I also checked for a stale mutant in bytecode: the in-tree __pycache__ .pyc files for auth_service and auth_routes decompile to the same bytecode as a fresh compile of the current sources. All later runs used PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX in the scratchpad plus PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE.

**Diff against the rulings.** Each ruling is implemented as written:
- W1-4b: the type classifier covers AuthRetryableError, httpx.TransportError, AuthApiError with status 429 or >= 500, and AuthUnknownError via original_error or __context__. The measured fact that original_error is the JSONDecodeError holds: mutant N_drop___context__ kills 429_html and 500_html. It is scoped to refresh_session only.
- W1-4c: the anon options are built locally with the constructor on both branches. Probe I shows they differ from create_client's default options ONLY in auto_refresh_token and persist_session. change_user_password now leaves 0 timers (probe H).
- Logout, flag ON: admin.sign_out(access, 'local') through asyncio.to_thread. The to_thread deviation from run_db is justified, since run_db is also to_thread when on but inline when off.
- Ruling 2: an expired bearer plus a refresh token rotates and then signs out locally, off-loop. With the flag OFF the original 401 is re-raised unchanged.
- W1-9b: SET NX EX + INCR, and a re-arm on TTL <= 0. The real upstash-redis 1.7.0 client, driven against a loopback REST fake (probe D), sends exactly ["SET",k,0,"NX","EX",900],["INCR",k], then ["GET",k],["TTL",k],["EXPIRE",k,900] and returns retry_after 900.

**CRLF and lint.** Every file is 100% CRLF and numstat shows line-level hunks only, no whole-file rewrites. ruff (E9,F63,F7,F82) and py_compile are clean.

**Mutations.** 32 mutants ran from byte snapshots, each with a sha256-verified restore; the harness asserted every restore; guard attempts were 0. The green's M1, M4, M5, M6, M8, M9, M12, M13, M14, M15, M21, M22, M23, M24, M26 and the reviewer's M7 and M9 were all re-killed with the same failing nodes. Among the new mutants these were killed:

**Unhappy paths through the real functions.**
- Probe A (the major defect): the flag-ON expired branch is an unauthenticated, unthrottled path to gotrue POST /token, 40 of 40, while /auth/refresh 429s after 10.
- Probes B and C (the minor defect): the remaining TTL-less counter paths.
- Probe E: with the flag ON, an expired bearer with a text/plain JSON-looking body is accepted (200 plus rotation), where a valid bearer with text/plain gets 422. This is harmless but inconsistent, and is related to the out-of-scope 422 follow-up.
- Probe G, more shapes: 501 and 505 give 503; 504 gives 503; 408 gives 503 via the pre-existing substring 'timeout'; 499 gives 401.
